Task: Outline and partially script a 15-minute educational video on climate change.

15-Minute Educational Video on Climate Change  
Working title: “Climate Change: The Problem, the Proof, the Possibilities”

—————————————
0. OVERVIEW FOR THE PRODUCER
—————————————
Goal     → Give a concise, hopeful, science-based primer that leaves viewers empowered.  
Audience  → General public, 15 +.  
Style   → Fast-paced, visually rich, narrator-led with on-camera experts, motion graphics, minimal jargon.  
Assets   → Stock footage, animated infographics, 2 expert sound-bites (scientist & community leader), royalty-free music bed.

—————————————
1. STRUCTURE AT A GLANCE (15:00)
—————————————
00:00–00:30  Cold-open hook  
00:30–02:00  What is climate change?  
02:00–05:00  The science: how we know  
05:00–08:00  Impacts already here  
08:00–11:30  Solutions & innovations  
11:30–13:30  What you can do  
13:30–15:00  Closing & call to hope  

—————————————
2. DETAILED OUTLINE WITH PARTIAL SCRIPT
—————————————
Time-code  Visuals                 Narration / Dialogue (partial script)

00:00–00:10  Montage: extreme weather clips, satellites, kids in classroom.  
Narrator (V.O.)  
“Floods in Europe, fires in Australia, record heat on every continent… It’s easy to feel overwhelmed.”

00:10–00:30  Title card animates on, warm but urgent music swell.  
“Yet right now, we hold the solutions in our own hands. Welcome to ‘Climate Change: The Problem, the Proof, the Possibilities.’”

— CHAPTER 1 — WHAT IS CLIMATE CHANGE? —
00:30–01:00  Simple globe animation showing greenhouse effect.  
“Climate change is the long-term shift in Earth’s average weather patterns, driven mainly by rising greenhouse gases—like wrapping the planet in an ever-thickening blanket.”

01:00–02:00  Quick cuts: smokestacks, cars, cows, deforestation drone shot.  
“Since the Industrial Revolution we’ve burned enough coal, oil and gas to raise CO₂ levels 50 %. That carbon traps heat; Earth has warmed about 1.2 °C already.”

Lower-third graphic: CO₂ 280 ppm → 421 ppm.

— CHAPTER 2 — HOW WE KNOW —
02:00–02:40  Scientist on-camera in lab holding ice core.  
Dr. Lee:  
“These bubbles are ancient air. They prove today’s CO₂ is higher than at any time in 800,000 years.”

02:40–03:30  Graph animation: temperature & CO₂ rise together.  
Narrator:  
“You don’t need to trust one graph. We have 150+ independent lines of evidence: rising sea levels, retreating glaciers, shifting plant zones.”

03:30–05:00  Split-screen montage: coral bleaching, satellite temps, blooming dates.  
“Different data, same story: the planet is warming—and we are the cause.”

— CHAPTER 3 — IMPACTS ALREADY HERE —
05:00–05:30  Home footage of flooded neighborhood.  
Narrator:  
“Heavier rains—because warmer air holds more moisture.”

05:30–06:15  Animation: jet stream wobble → heat domes.  
“Heat waves are now hotter, longer, deadlier.”

06:15–07:00  Graphic map: wildfire seasons lengthen.  
“Fire seasons in the U.S. West are two months longer than 50 years ago.”

07:00–08:00  Interview: Community leader Maria Gomez in coastal town.  
Maria:  
“We lost our playground to the sea. But we’re building back smarter—elevated and powered by solar.”

— CHAPTER 4 — SOLUTIONS & INNOVATIONS —
08:00–08:45  Rapid-fire shots: offshore wind farm, rooftop solar, electric buses.  
Narrator:  
“Clean energy is now often the cheapest energy.”

08:45–09:30  Animation: drawdown wedges (efficiency, renewables, reforestation, food).  
“Four big levers can get us most of the way: efficiency, clean power, protecting forests, and better food systems.”

09:30–10:30  Factory floor: workers building batteries.  
Engineer voice-over:  
“Battery costs fell 89 % in a decade. That’s why electric cars are exploding in sales—figuratively, not literally.”

10:30–11:30  Side-by-side: regenerative farm & vertical urban farm.  
Narrator:  
“Healthy soils store carbon. Eating less meat and cutting food waste could erase 8 % of global emissions.”

— CHAPTER 5 — WHAT YOU CAN DO —
11:30–12:15  Infographic “Personal Carbon Smashers”: vote, swap bulbs, ditch short flights, plant trees.  
Narrator:  
“Individual action amplifies systemic change. Start with the big three: how you power your home, how you move, what you eat.”

12:15–13:00  Street vox-pop: students lobbying city council.  
Student:  
“We pushed our school district to get electric buses. It worked!”

13:00–13:30  Quick recap overlay.  
Narrator:  
“When millions act, politicians follow, markets shift, and the sky—quite literally—gets clearer.”

— CHAPTER 6 — CLOSING & CALL TO HOPE —
13:30–14:30  Return to scientist & community leader in split-screen.  
Dr. Lee:  
“Every tenth of a degree matters. The sooner we cut emissions, the more future we save.”  
Maria:  
“We’re proof: resilience and justice can go hand in hand.”

14:30–15:00  Sunset drone shot of wind turbines; upbeat music rise.  
Narrator:  
“This story isn’t written yet. You’re holding the pen. Let’s write a cooler, brighter chapter—together.”  
On-screen text: “Act now. climateaction.org”  
Fade out.

—————————————
3. PRODUCTION NOTES
—————————————
• Voice & Pace: Conversational, optimistic, 140–150 words per minute.  
• Graphics Package: Color palette (#0077be teal, #f9a825 gold) + rounded sans-serif fonts.  
• Music: Mid-tempo soundtrack, dip under dialogue, optimistic uplift at 08:00 & 14:30.  
• Accessibility: Closed captions, audio descriptions for diagrams.  
• Deliverables: 4K master, 60-second trailer, 15-sec TikTok cut-downs.

—————————————
